results.title: Why the Nvidia scandal is bad news for Europe’s AI ambitions
results.content: Nvidia's Jensen Huang poured money into open-source AI, from French-founded Hugging Face to chips for Mistral's data centres, and fought Washington's attempts to restrict it. With Huang gone and China hawks emboldened, Tech 24 asks whether Europe's AI ambitions have lost their most powerful ally, and whether he was ever the champion Europe needed.

results.title: US probes nationwide flights stoppage as travel disruptions persist
results.content: US air travel is expected to return to normal this Sunday, following a nationwide ground stop Friday night that stranded hundreds of thousands of passengers and disrupted travel worldwide. The Trump administration blamed the incident on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines and said there was no evidence this was a cyberattack. The ground stop now raises questions about the country's aging infrastructure and lawmakers are calling for an investigation. Analysis by Philip Mann, aviation expert at Vector Strategic Consulting.

results.title: Chinese spy, chip sales, Trump ties... The Nvidia scandal deepens
results.content: The Nvidia scandal continues to unravel. Sunday, the Singapore-based company Megaspeed said that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang had officially left the company in 2025. She is the alleged Chinese spy that had an affair with Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. Late last year, revelations showed she was being investigated for chip smuggling. The scandal has also raised questions about how much the US government knew – Trump was allegedly warned about the affair but did not react. Analysis by Laïla Mörch, CEO of Shael and tech investor in Paris.

results.title: The week in pictures: Spain protests, Pope Leo's Peru 'homecoming' and Rocky fans in Philly
results.content: FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images, from angry protests over a housing crisis that has dominated Spain's election campaign, to Leo XIV's visit to his adopted homeland Peru and "Rocky" fans marking 50 years since the release of boxing movie classic.

results.title: French Cyril Gane retains MMA heavyweaight title agianst Josh Hokit
results.content: Ciryl Gane remains the world's MMA heavyweight champion. Overnight, the French athlete beat Josh Hokit in the main event of UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden in ​New York. The 5-round fight was rough, as Shirli Sitbon explains.

results.title: Bahrain says air defences destroyed several Iranian drones attacking US base
results.content: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September. The second Iranian drone attack in three days, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East war. Diplomatic efforts to end the almost nine-month conflict have yet to produce a breakthrough, with ​sporadic attacks continuing. Details from the ground by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Tehran, Reza Sayah.

results.title: France's presidential race heats up
results.content: In approximately six months time, French voters will head to the polls for the first round of the presidential election. Due to term limits, current president Emmanuel Macron is barred from running again. But that hasn't stopped a whole host of candidates from tossing their hat in the ring.

results.title: Ukrainian drones strike Russia's petrochemical capital in overnight assault
results.content: Russian officials confirmed Sunday that the central industrial city of Nizhnekamsk had endured "prolonged" Ukrainian airstrikes overnight, damaging a residential building and sparking a fire at a major petrochemical complex, injuring three people. Separate overnight strikes on Taganrog city killed an electricity substation engineer, according to the regional governor.

results.title: The Philippines and Australia strengthen joint military deterrence at ASEAN summit
results.content: Southeast Asian leaders opened their annual summit in the Philippine capital Manila on Sunday. During three days, world leaders are expected to focus on trade, energy and conflict – including the war in Iran. Donald Trump is expected to land in Manila on Tuesday. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Bangkok Tommy Walker.

results.title: Will Ukraine make territorial concessions for NATO membership?
results.content: The United States suggested Ukraine make territorial concessions in exchange for a NATO membership, according to Volodymyr Zelensky. The Ukrainian president also claims that Russia has rejected an energy truce. This week’s US-mediated negotiations did not result in any tangible progress. Story by Simon Moritz.

results.title: Air travel issues persist in the US after nationwide ground stop
results.content: After almost five hours of grounded flights in the US, flights have resumed. However, passengers are still waiting and wading through tough logistics to get to their destinations after massive delays and cancelled flights. Details by Simon Moritz.

results.title: Francophone summit opens in Cambodia, overshadowed by tensions in Africa
results.content: The 20th Francophonie Summit opened on Sunday in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, overshadowed by a high-stakes leadership dispute. The International Organisation of the Francophonie is set to elect its next secretary-general on Monday for a four-year term, but escalating friction between Rwanda, which has led the OIF for eight years, and the Democratic Republic of Congo has thrown the summit into crisis. Details by Liza Kaminov.

results.title: Illegal mining threatens French Guiana forests and indigenous communities
results.content: In French Guiana, the fight against illegal gold mining is rapidly being lost and creating an environmental and health disaster, according to the World Wildlife Fund. During an aerial survey in early August, park rangers counted 239 illegal sites within the protected area in record.

results.title: Are we too reliant on technology? Questions arise after Microsoft's widespread outages
results.content: This week's Microsoft outage highlighted the risks of relying on a single technology provider for essential services. The disruption lasted nearly 24 hours, impacting millions of users across more than 70 countries – from government agencies to airlines to hospitals and small businesses. Are we too reliant on technology? Analysis by Marcel Saucet, research associate at the University of San Diego School of Law.

results.title: Pope laments poverty-stricken Inca communities as locals leave Peru
results.content: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday will traverse the length of Peru in what marks the penultimate day of his Latin American tour. The leader of the Catholic church – who underwent cancer surgery just a month ago – warned that Peru's remote Inca communities are under threat as poverty continues to drive locals out of their homeland in search of better futures.

results.title: Global diesel prices ease as winter approaches
results.content: Global diesel prices, which have remained elevated since the start of the Iran war and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, have fallen sharply in recent weeks as Gulf exports recover and global oil supplies get back on track for the first time since February. The price drop is being felt in Europe, where prices remain roughly 77% above pre-war levels, and in the US, where the national average fell below $6 a gallon on Saturday. Details by Liza Kaminov.

results.title: Philippine star Carmelle wins first Asian edition of Eurovision song contest
results.content: The Philippines has won the first Asian edition of the Eurovision Song Contest. The Filipino singer beat ten other acts to take the title in Bangkok, with a song celebrating women's empowerment. A taste of the winning song with Jack Pownall.

results.title: Iran claims attack on US military airbase in Bahrain
results.content: Iranian military confirmed on Sunday an attack on a US military base in Bahrain, in its second targeting the Middle Eastern country in the space of three days. Bahrain's military said it had intercepted several Iranian attacks, with the foreign ministry confirming its air defence systems had shot down Iranian drones, preventing them from reaching their intended targets.

results.title: SpaceX makes rocketry history by recapturing massive reusable rocketship
results.content: After failing to catch a booster yesterday, SpaceX managed to recapture its massive reusable rocketship, "Starship" for the first time. Smaller previous models have successfully relanded but they require heavy legs and aren't fully reusable. Story by Daniel Quinlan.

results.title: Zinédine Zidane returns to Bordeaux as France take on Turkey in Nations League
results.content: France will need to avoid defeat against Turkey, who they face in Bordeaux on Sunday night, to seal their spot in this season's Nations League quarter-finals. The match will see head coach Zinédine Zidane return to the city in which he spent four seasons as a player.

results.title: Three sentenced to death over Jordan church attack
results.content: A Jordanian court on Sunday sentenced the three gunmen responsible for a terror attack on a church funeral procession in the village of Hamoud that killed nine and wounded others. The attack prompted retaliatory strikes on "terrorist organisations" in neighbouring Syria.

results.title: Cape Verde could make election history with first female president
results.content: Cape Verde goes to the polls on Sunday in an election that could see the African island nation appoint its first ever female leader. Justice Minister Joana Rosa challenges incumbent Jose Maria Neves, who is the country's fifth president since it became independent from Portugal in 1975.

results.title: 'Is this a cyberattack?' Grounded flights, a Microsoft outage and AI chaos fuel cybersecurity fears
results.content: A series of unsettling disruptions, from tech stock turbulence and Microsoft outages to a nationwide grounding of flights, has left millions wondering whether the world’s increasingly interconnected technology systems are beginning to unravel.

results.title: SpaceX's Starship completes first-ever mid-air catch after return from orbit
results.content: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft made a successful return to Earth on Saturday, completing its first mid-air catch by giant robot arms in Texas, after an aborted recovery attempt.
